bottom_line: Dalcetrapib — dal-GenE. Stated failure: Phase III: primary intention-to-treat cardiovascular endpoint not significant. Diagnosis (claim 1.3, supported): The registry primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and non-fatal stroke; dalcetrapib vs control HR was 0.88 (95% CI 0.75–1.03), p=0.12, so the primary endpoint was missed.
lines: [1] dal-GenE tested dalcetrapib in a genotype-defined ADCY9-selected population as a post-failure precision-medicine hypothesis after dal-OUTCOMES failed in 2012. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[2] The curated record states dal-GenE still missed the primary intention-to-treat endpoint and that plausible post hoc precision-medicine findings may not confirm. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[3] The registry primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and non-fatal stroke; dalcetrapib vs control HR was 0.88 (95% CI 0.75–1.03), p=0.12, so the primary endpoint was missed. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[4] The registry secondary composite including hospitalization for ACS or unanticipated coronary revascularization showed HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.88–1.13), p=0.95. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[5] The registry secondary composite including hospitalization for new or worsening heart failure showed HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.79–1.07), p=0.27. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[6] No registry fact states that dal-GenE was stopped early; the facts only report the 2022 readout and missed primary ITT endpoint. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov, curated record; record types: registry, curated; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[7] Retrospective pharmacogenomics suggested an ADCY9-defined responder group in dal-GenE. (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[8] dal-GenE still missed the primary intention-to-treat endpoint (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.75-1.03, p=0.12). (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[9] The genotype-defined subgroup finding did not rescue dalcetrapib; dal-GenE missed its primary ITT endpoint. (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: curated record, ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: curated, registry; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[10] dal-GenE (NCT02525939) tested dalcetrapib in Acute Coronary Syndrome. (section: Related Indications; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[11] ADCY9 is associated with response to dalcetrapib, suggesting a genotype-defined pharmacogenomic signal. (section: Related Indications; sources: ClinPGx (PharmGKB); record types: database; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[12] Dalcetrapib interacts with Cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP), and CETP is associated with acute coronary syndrome. (section: Related Indications; sources: ChEMBL, Open Targets Platform, MONDO; record types: curated, database; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: moderate; check: supported by its cited records).

[13] ADCY9 is associated with response to dalcetrapib. (section: Related Indications; sources: ClinPGx (PharmGKB); record types: database; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[14] A retrospective pharmacogenomic analysis suggested an ADCY9-defined responder group for dalcetrapib. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[15] dal-GenE was a genotype-selected phase III trial testing that ADCY9-defined hypothesis. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).
question: Did a genotype-defined population rescue dalcetrapib in dal-GenE?
raw: No. dal-GenE tested dalcetrapib in an ADCY9-selected genotype-defined population as a post hoc precision-medicine hypothesis after dal-OUTCOMES failed [1, 15]. The registry primary ITT endpoint was missed (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.75–1.03, p=0.12) [3, 8]. Retrospective pharmacogenomics suggested an ADCY9-defined responder group [7, 14], but this is hypothesis-generating and did not rescue dalcetrapib [9]. Lines [11] and [13] report ADCY9 response associations from ClinPGx/PharmGKB; [12] is a curated database summary of CETP interactions. No line shows confirmation of the subgroup signal or trial success.
